clue.text: Part of a vehicle from which assistance is forthcoming

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words that follow, the answer being drawn out of which assistance

explanation.surface: A car part that somehow dispenses help to the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' says the answer is drawn out of the run 'which assistance', which spans the end of 'which' and the start of 'assistance'; 'is forthcoming' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassis is the base frame of a car or lorry on which the body is mounted.

clue.text: MP caught by whip — hard cheese? Not so

indicators.note: being caught means being held inside, so the politician word sits within the whip

parts.note: a cat, the cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A party whip nabs an MP, and the MP's bad luck is shrugged off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck; here it misleads: the cheese is soft, hence 'Not so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, the opposite of a hard one.

clue.text: Drink can make a man unfriendly, hard-hearted

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the heart, the middle, of the word for unfriendly

parts.note: cool means unfriendly, distant
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Drinking can turn a man cold and callous.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is a general term for intoxicating drink.

clue.text: Be relieved it can give you a good time

definitions.meaning: to come off guard duty, ending one's spell on watch

definitions.text: it can give you a good time
definitions.meaning: a timer used to measure a fast time in a race

explanation.surface: Relief is followed by the promise of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop watch is to end a sentry duty; a stopwatch times races precisely.

clue.text: Needled card-players

definitions.meaning: stitched with a needle and thread
in bridge the four players are known as South, East, West and North

explanation.surface: Card-players getting irritated with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needled' looks like annoyed; it means stitched. The bridge seats are given by their compass initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn means stitched, worked with a needle and thread.

clue.text: Nothing planted in garden area is so precious

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' meaning love comes from tennis scoring, where zero is called love; 'planted in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is dearly loved and held dear, a darling.

clue.text: Biscuit in tub underfed boy wanted

parts.note: a bath is a tub
Oliver Twist, the hungry workhouse boy, asked for more

explanation.surface: A hungry boy in the bath longs for a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan who famously asks for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is a plain dry English cracker invented by a doctor in Bath.

clue.text: Lover of Ridd — name author originally made up

definitions.meaning: John Ridd is the hero of R. D. Blackmore's novel, and the heroine is his beloved
a first name said to have been coined by Blackmore for his heroine

explanation.surface: A romantic heroine whose name was the novelist's own invention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna Doone, heroine of the 1869 novel, is loved by John Ridd; Blackmore is credited with coining the name.

clue.text: Wild flower spreading round end of garden

indicators.note: something spreading round encloses, so the flower goes about the letter

parts.note: a violet is a flower

indicators.note: the end of garden is its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild flower' looks like one phrase; 'Wild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent means fierce or uncontrolled, as in a violent storm.

clue.text: Football — first or second half

parts.note: split the word into its halves; to foot it means to ..., and a ball is a formal ...

explanation.definitionFit: Footing it is dancing, and a ball is a social occasion for dancing.

clue.text: Asian city about to be captured by Chinese leader

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside, so the short word sits within the leader's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong led communist China
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A city on the China coast falls to the forces of Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: Macao is the former Portuguese enclave on the south China coast, now a special administrative region.

clue.text: Thin as result of drought?

definitions.meaning: to dilute a drink or weaken a statement
read literally, in a drought the water level is down

explanation.surface: Cryptic quip linking dilution to a dry spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To water down is to dilute; in a drought water supplies are literally lowered.

clue.text: Indian in part of US, a belligerent type

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for Missouri, a US state
a hawk is someone who favours war, the opposite of a dove

explanation.surface: A warlike Native American found in one of the states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means a Native American; MO for Missouri is the US postal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Mark in Latin can be beaten by no beginner

indicators.note: the short word is the beginner, so it goes at the front of what follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word beaten is something that can be reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Latin note on a page that a novice could never better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges BEATEN into TABENE, and 'by no beginner' puts NO first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene, Latin for note well, is a marginal sign telling a reader to take special notice.

clue.text: Comfortable way in which to live?

definitions.text: Comfortable way in which to live?

parts.words: Comfortable way in which to live?
parts.note: the idiom for prosperous living, read as a soft, easy road one might reside on

explanation.definitionFit: To live on the idiomatic road of ease means to be well off and free of worry.

clue.text: Story retracted about Conservative success in Paris

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A Tory withdraws a tale after a triumph in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' turns TALE into ELAT; 'about' puts that round C to give E-C-LAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is a French borrowing meaning brilliant success or acclaim, hence 'in Paris'.

clue.text: Man in a taxi ordered cab originally — that's self-evident

indicators.note: the island abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word cab

explanation.surface: A man gets into a taxi he ordered, which goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges A TAXI, and 'in' puts the Isle of Man abbreviation within the result; 'originally' takes the first letter of 'cab'.
explanation.definitionFit: Axiomatic describes a truth so obvious it needs no proof.

clue.text: Complex plan to get chap work across the Channel

parts.note: a chap is a man
oeuvre is French for work, France lying across the English Channel

explanation.surface: A man plans an elaborate project in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A manoeuvre is a scheme or skilful move to gain an end.

clue.text: Lamenting cricket side's withdrawal

parts.note: crying means weeping, lamenting
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team mourns as it pulls out of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying off is backing out of an arrangement.

clue.text: To operate keys so expertly takes a little class

parts.note: a touch is a small amount, as in a touch of salt
a type is a kind or class

explanation.surface: A good typist only needs a short lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch-type is to type without looking at the keyboard, using all fingers.

clue.text: Not giving complete satisfaction in a duel, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunate events go awry, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: King expelled from kingdom? Certainly not!

parts.note: Norway is a Scandinavian kingdom
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is thrown out of his realm, and someone protests.

clue.text: Conductor said to live in accordance with aspirations

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the conductor's name is judged by sound

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood founded the Proms concerts
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A conductor talks of living up to one's ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood was a British conductor, founder of the Proms concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Would-be describes someone aspiring to a role, as in a would-be actor.

clue.text: Permits needed on journey for groups of children arriving together

indicators.note: one word is placed on, that is after, the other

parts.note: a trip is a journey
lets means permits, allows

explanation.surface: Travel documents required for a family trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplets are three children born at one birth, so each set is a trio arriving at once.

clue.text: It would be an advantage if this girl turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: an asset is an advantage

explanation.surface: Her arrival would be welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a girl's name.

clue.text: Deposit consisting of gold initially found in vein

indicators.note: one piece is found inside another, so the letter sits within the vein

parts.note: a lode is a vein of ore

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a mining noun; it is the verb, to lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to deposit, as in lodging money or a complaint.

clue.text: Sort of ticket needed for election

definitions.meaning: a ticket for a journey out and back
the result of a vote, as when an MP is ... to Parliament

explanation.surface: A double definition joined by a link phrase.

clue.text: Book collection to absorb

parts.note: a lot is a collection, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A book collector sops up knowledge.

clue.text: Half of the capital needed to make this film

explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film or programme.

clue.text: Complaint from porter resulted in hearing

indicators.note: a hearing means listening, so the words are judged by sound

clue.text: Legally concerning that ring held by the judge

O is a ring by shape
